sources.text: Paracetamol, also known as acetaminophen, is a medication used to treat fever and mild to moderate pain. Common brand names include Tylenol and Panadol. name: boil-verbatim
q: How long should I boil water to make it safe?

sources.title: Boiling water
sources.text: Boiling is the most reliable way to kill germs in water. Bring the water to a rolling boil for 1 minute. At altitudes above 2,000 m (6,500 ft), boil for 3 minutes. Let the water cool naturally and store it in a clean, covered container. Boiling does not remove chemicals such as lead, nitrates or pesticides.

sources.title: Water chlorination
sources.text: Chlorine bleach can be used when boiling is not possible. Use unscented household bleach of 5–6% strength. Add 2 drops of bleach per litre of clear water, or 4 drops per litre if the water is cloudy or very cold. Stir and wait at least 30 minutes before drinking. The water should have a slight chlorine smell; if not, repeat the dose and wait another 15 minutes.

sources.title: Solar water disinfection
sources.text: Solar water disinfection (SODIS) uses sunlight to kill germs in clear water. Fill clear plastic PET bottles of up to 2 litres and lay them in full sun for at least 6 hours. On cloudy days the bottles need 2 consecutive days. SODIS does not work on rainy days or with cloudy water, which should be filtered first.

name: chain-verbatim
q: When should I replace an 11-speed chain?

sources.title: Bicycle Chain Replacement - iFixit
sources.text: Step 1: Shift the chain onto the smallest cog at the back and the smallest chainring at the front. Step 2: Measure chain wear with a chain checker; replace an 11-speed chain when wear reaches 0.5%. Step 3: Use a chain tool to push out a pin, or open the quick link with quick-link pliers. Step 4: Lay the new chain beside the old one and cut it to the same number of links. Step 5: Join the chain with a new quick link, then pedal backwards to check that it runs smoothly. Never reuse a pin that has been pushed out of an 11-speed chain.

name: mom-three-parts
q: How do I get around Mombasa?

sources.title: Mombasa
sources.text: Matatus (minibuses) are the cheapest way to get around and cost 50–100 KSh for a trip within the city. Tuk-tuks are common and a short ride costs about 150–300 KSh; agree on the price before you get in. Boda-bodas (motorbike taxis) are fast but accidents are frequent, so ask for a helmet. The Likoni ferry crosses to the south coast every 20 minutes and is free for foot passengers. Taxis from Moi International Airport to the city centre cost about 1,500 KSh. Ride-hailing apps such as Uber and Bolt operate in Mombasa.

sources.title: iPhone 8
sources.text: Repair information and guides for the iPhone 8 that was released on September 22, 2017. Use this guide to revive your iPhone 8’s... Learn how to replace your iPhone 8 screen. The successor to the iPhone 7, the iPhone 8 (as well as the 8 Plus and X) was formally announced by Apple on September 12, 2017. The most often replaced iPhone 8 parts include the battery, screen, and home button. You can identify the iPhone 8 by finding one of the model numbers either on the inner edge of the SIM card tray or within the phone's Settings app: The iPhone 8 features a 4.7 in (diagonal) glass screen with curved edges, a white or black bezel, and a home button. The iPhone 8 can be differentiated from the iPhone 8 Plus by its 4.7 in diagonal screen (relative to the 5.5 in screen of the Plus model). The iPhone 8 can be differentiated from the iPhone SE 2020 & 2022 (2nd and 3rd Gen) by its back cover. Diagnose any issues you may be having with your iPhone 8 using our iPhone 8 Troubleshooting Page.

sources.title: iPhone 8 Battery Replacement
sources.text: This is a prerequisite-only guide to replace the battery in an iPhone 8. Opening the iPhone 8 will damage the waterproof seals on the display. Step 1: The iPhone's battery is secured by four pieces of stretch-release adhesive—two at the top, and two at the bottom. Be careful not to poke the battery with any sharp tools. Step 3: Slowly pull one battery adhesive tab away from the battery, towards the bottom of the iPhone. Step 4: Be sure to hold onto the battery as you remove the final strip, or it may fling out of the iPhone unexpectedly. Step 5: If you choose to use pry tools to lift the battery out of the iPhone, use extreme caution or you may damage the ribbon cables or the wireless charging coil directly underneath the battery. Don't overheat the iPhone, or you may accidentally ignite the battery. Step 6: Remove the battery from the iPhone. Step 6: If your replacement battery came in a plastic sleeve, slide off and remove the sleeve before installation. Repair didn’t go as planned?

sources.text: Kiambu is a major town and the capital of Kiambu County, located just north of Nairobi in Kenya. sources.title: Paracetamol
sources.text: Paracetamol, also known as acetaminophen, is a medication used to treat fever and mild to moderate pain. Common brand names include Tylenol and Panadol. The typical adult dose is 500 mg to 1 g every 4 to 6 hours, up to a maximum of 4 g in 24 hours. In children the dose is 10 to 15 mg per kg of body weight every 4 to 6 hours, with no more than 5 doses in 24 hours. Taking more than the maximum daily dose can cause liver failure. If an overdose is suspected, seek medical help immediately, even if the person feels well. People with liver disease or who drink alcohol heavily should use a lower dose.

sources.title: Boiling water
sources.text: Boiling is the most reliable way to kill germs in water. Bring the water to a rolling boil for 1 minute. At altitudes above 2,000 m (6,500 ft), boil for 3 minutes. Let the water cool naturally and store it in a clean, covered container. Boiling does not remove chemicals such as lead, nitrates or pesticides.

sources.title: Water chlorination
sources.text: Chlorine bleach can be used when boiling is not possible. Use unscented household bleach of 5–6% strength. Add 2 drops of bleach per litre of clear water, or 4 drops per litre if the water is cloudy or very cold. Stir and wait at least 30 minutes before drinking. The water should have a slight chlorine smell; if not, repeat the dose and wait another 15 minutes.

name: r-hypo-symptoms
q: What are the symptoms of mild hypothermia?

sources.title: Hypothermia
sources.text: Hypothermia is defined as a body core temperature below 35.0 °C (95.0 °F). Mild hypothermia is 32–35 °C, moderate is 28–32 °C and severe is below 28 °C. Symptoms of mild hypothermia include shivering and confusion; in severe hypothermia shivering stops. Remove wet clothing and warm the person gradually with blankets. Do not rub the arms and legs, and do not put the person in a hot bath. Paradoxical undressing, in which a person removes their clothing, occurs in 20 to 50% of deaths from hypothermia.

sources.title: iPhone 8
sources.text: Repair information and guides for the iPhone 8 that was released on September 22, 2017. Use this guide to revive your iPhone 8’s... Learn how to replace your iPhone 8 screen. The successor to the iPhone 7, the iPhone 8 (as well as the 8 Plus and X) was formally announced by Apple on September 12, 2017. The most often replaced iPhone 8 parts include the battery, screen, and home button. You can identify the iPhone 8 by finding one of the model numbers either on the inner edge of the SIM card tray or within the phone's Settings app: The iPhone 8 features a 4.7 in (diagonal) glass screen with curved edges, a white or black bezel, and a home button. The iPhone 8 can be differentiated from the iPhone 8 Plus by its 4.7 in diagonal screen (relative to the 5.5 in screen of the Plus model). The iPhone 8 can be differentiated from the iPhone SE 2020 & 2022 (2nd and 3rd Gen) by its back cover. Diagnose any issues you may be having with your iPhone 8 using our iPhone 8 Troubleshooting Page.

sources.title: iPhone 8 Battery Replacement
sources.text: This is a prerequisite-only guide to replace the battery in an iPhone 8. Opening the iPhone 8 will damage the waterproof seals on the display. Step 1: The iPhone's battery is secured by four pieces of stretch-release adhesive—two at the top, and two at the bottom. Be careful not to poke the battery with any sharp tools. Step 3: Slowly pull one battery adhesive tab away from the battery, towards the bottom of the iPhone. Step 4: Be sure to hold onto the battery as you remove the final strip, or it may fling out of the iPhone unexpectedly. Step 5: If you choose to use pry tools to lift the battery out of the iPhone, use extreme caution or you may damage the ribbon cables or the wireless charging coil directly underneath the battery. Don't overheat the iPhone, or you may accidentally ignite the battery. Step 6: Remove the battery from the iPhone. Step 6: If your replacement battery came in a plastic sleeve, slide off and remove the sleeve before installation. Repair didn’t go as planned?
